Raosaheb Adhav vs The State Of Maharashtra on 8 September, 2020 Author: V.L.Achliya Bench: V.L.Achliya 692.20ABA.odt 1 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad 936 Anticipatory Bail Application No.692 Of 2020 Sambhaji S/O.Raosaheb Adhav Versus The State Of Maharashtra ... Mr.G.R.Syed, Advocate for the applicant. Mr.N.T.Bhagat, App for the respondent-State. ... CORAM : V.L.ACHLIYA,J. DATE : 08.09.2020 P.C. 1] The applicant - accused has moved this application seeking anticipatory bail on an apprehension of arrest in connection with the offences registered u/s. 188, 272, 273, 328, 34 of the IPC and u/s. 26 [2] [6], 27 [2] [E], 30 [2] [A] r/w. 59 [6] of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, vide C.R. No. 454/2019 with Nanalpeth Police Station, Parbhani.
texts.facts: no.1 for carriage of the passengers . The vehicle was inspected by police at Parbhani. At the time of inspection it was found that 24 bags of Gutka containing Goa 100 pouches worth Rs.3,24,480/- transported by said vehicle. The alleged seizure was made in between the night of 25.10.2019 and 26.10.2019. However, the first information report was lodged on 01.11.2019 against Shaikh Farooque Ahmed Shaikh Iqbal, the person who was driving the vehicle and Sambhaji S/O. Raosaheb Adhav vs The State Of Maharashtra on 8 September, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145034145/ 2 ::: Uploaded on - 09/09/2020 ::: Downloaded on - 10/09/2020 03:37: 692.20ABA.odt 3 carrying alleged contraband article [Gutka]. The name of the applicant not mentioned in the First Information Report.
texts.arguments: In brief, it is the contention of the learned counsel for the applicant that the entire accusation against the applicant is without basis. The applicant is implicated in the case only for the reason the vehicle in which alleged contraband article i.e. Gutka was seized owned by the applicant. It is contended that the applicant is running travel agency at Shrigonda, Dist. Ahmednagar. The vehicle in question was taken by the accused 4] By referring allegations made in the first information report, learned counsel submits that there is no prima facie case to establish that the alleged contraband articles were carried with the direction or with the knowledge of the applicant. It is further submitted that the offences u/s. 188, 272, 273 and 328 of the IPC are not attracted against the applicant as he was not present when those articles were seized. He was not in physical possession of said contraband articles. For the offences punishable u/s.59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the maximum sentence provided not more than 6 months. The prime accused in the case has been arrested and released on regular bail. 5] On the other hand, learned APP Sambhaji S/O.
